orig_text: ITR MUST set the 'EID HMAC ID' field to 0 before computing the HMAC.
correct_text: ITR MUST set the 'EID HMAC' field to 0 before computing the HMAC.
notes: 0 (zero) must be set in the 'EID HMAC' field, not in the 'EID HMAC ID' field

orig_text:
A KDF value of NONE (0) may be used to specify that the ITR has no
   preferred KDF ID.
correct_text:
A KDF value of NOPREF (0) may be used to specify that the ITR has no
   preferred KDF ID.
notes:
Section 8.5 of this document ("Key Derivation Functions") registers
value 0 with the name "NOPREF", and Section 6.2 uses "A KDF value of
NOPREF (0)" with that meaning.  Using the name "NONE" here for the same
registry value is inconsistent and may confuse implementers checking
the IANA registry.

orig_text:
If the ITR did indicate a Requested HMAC ID in the Map-Request and the PKT HAMC ID in the
corresponding Map-Reply is different, or if the ITR did not indicate a Requested HMAC ID in the
Map-Request and the PKT HMAC ID in the corresponding Map-Reply is not supported, then the ITR
MUST discard the Map-Reply and send, according to rate-limitation policies defined in [RFC9301],
a new Map-Request with a different 'Requested HMAC ID' field, according to ITR's local policy.
correct_text:
If the ITR did indicate a Requested HMAC ID in the Map-Request and the PKT HMAC ID in the
corresponding Map-Reply is different, or if the ITR did not indicate a Requested HMAC ID in the
Map-Request and the PKT HMAC ID in the corresponding Map-Reply is not supported, then the ITR
MUST discard the Map-Reply and send, according to rate-limitation policies defined in [RFC9301],
a new Map-Request with a different 'Requested HMAC ID' field, according to ITR's local policy.
notes:
"HAMC" is a typographical error for "HMAC".  The acronym HMAC appears 91
times elsewhere in this document; "HAMC" appears only here (Section 6.9).

Verifier Notes: Updated text to include entire sentence.

orig_text:
OTK Length:  The length (in bytes) of the OTK Authentication Data
      (OTK-AD), which contains the OTK Preamble and the OTK.
correct_text:
OTK Length:  The length (in bytes) of the OTK Authentication Data
      (OTK-AD), which contains the OTK Length, Key ID, and OTK Wrapping
      ID fields, followed by the OTK Preamble and the One-Time Key.
notes:
Figure 1 draws the OTK-AD as covering the OTK Length, Key ID, and OTK
Wrapping ID fields as well as the OTK Preamble and the One-Time Key,
but this definition says that the OTK-AD contains only the OTK
Preamble and the OTK.  The EID-AD follows the other convention:
Section 6.4 sets the EID-AD Length to 4 bytes when it contains only
the 2-byte KDF ID field, and Section 6.9 measures the EID-AD from the
EID-AD Length field.  With a 128-bit OTK the definition yields 24
bytes while Figure 1 yields 28 bytes, which changes where the receiver
locates the start of the EID-AD.  The correction aligns the definition
with Figure 1 and with the EID-AD convention.

orig_text:
If the 'PKT HMAC ID' field does not match the Requested HMAC ID, the ITR
MUST discard the Map-Reply and send, according to rate-limitation
policies defined in [RFC9301], a new Map-Request with a different
Requested HMAC ID, according to ITR's local policy or until all HMAC
IDs supported by the ITR have been attempted.
correct_text:
If the ITR did indicate a Requested HMAC ID and the 'PKT HMAC ID' field is
different, or if the ITR did not indicate a Requested HMAC ID and
the 'PKT HMAC ID' field is not supported, the ITR MUST discard the
Map-Reply and send, according to rate-limitation policies defined in
[RFC9301], a new Map-Request with a different Requested HMAC ID,
according to ITR's local policy or until all HMAC IDs supported by
the ITR have been attempted.
notes:
This sentence requires discarding any Map-Reply whose 'PKT HMAC ID'
does not match the Requested HMAC ID, but Section 6.4 allows the ITR
to send NONE (0), meaning it has no preferred HMAC ID.  With 0 in the
Requested HMAC ID field, no registered PKT HMAC ID (1 or 2 in
Section 8.3) can match, so every Map-Reply would be discarded and
retried "until all HMAC IDs supported by the ITR have been attempted",
and the ITR could never accept a protected Map-Reply.  The preceding
paragraph of Section 6.9 uses a two-branch rule conditioned on whether
the ITR indicated a Requested HMAC ID.  The correction applies the
same two-branch structure to the PKT HMAC ID.

orig_text:
If the ITR did indicate a Requested HMAC ID in the Map-Request and
the PKT HAMC ID in the corresponding Map-Reply is different, or if
the ITR did not indicate a Requested HMAC ID in the Map-Request and
the PKT HMAC ID in the corresponding Map-Reply is not supported, then
the ITR MUST discard the Map-Reply and send, according to rate-
limitation policies defined in [RFC9301], a new Map-Request with a
different 'Requested HMAC ID' field, according to ITR's local policy.
correct_text:
If the ITR did indicate a Requested HMAC ID in the Map-Request and
the EID HMAC ID in the corresponding Map-Reply is different, or if
the ITR did not indicate a Requested HMAC ID in the Map-Request and
the EID HMAC ID in the corresponding Map-Reply is not supported, then
the ITR MUST discard the Map-Reply and send, according to rate-
limitation policies defined in [RFC9301], a new Map-Request with a
different 'Requested HMAC ID' field, according to ITR's local policy.
notes:
This paragraph verifies the EID-AD and names the 'EID HMAC ID' field
as the algorithm to use, but its discard condition compares the
Requested HMAC ID with the 'PKT HMAC ID' field.  The 'PKT HMAC ID'
identifies the algorithm protecting the PKT-AD, and that comparison is
specified separately later in this section.  As written, the
'EID HMAC ID' is never checked against the Requested HMAC ID, so a
Map-Server that substitutes a different algorithm (Section 6.7.1
permits this) goes unnoticed by the ITR.  The correction changes the
field name in this condition to 'EID HMAC ID'; the spelling "HAMC" in
the same sentence was already corrected by Errata ID 9226.

orig_text: | Record Count  |   Unassigned  |         EID HMAC ID           |EID-AD
correct_text: | Record Count  |E| Unassigned  |         EID HMAC ID           |EID-AD
notes:
Section 6.1 defines the ETR-Cant-Sign E bit in the EID-AD and states
that it signals to the ITR that at least one ETR that is authoritative
for the EID-Prefixes of this Map-Reply has not enabled LISP-SEC, and
Table 1 of Section 6.7 requires a Map-Server to set it to 1.  The ITR
only receives the Map-Reply, so the bit must be present in the
Map-Reply authentication data.  Figure 2 instead shows that octet as
an 8-bit "Unassigned" field that is set to 0 on transmission, so the
bit could not reach the ITR.  The correction restores the E bit in
Figure 2 (the layout already used in Figure 1) and adds a
corresponding entry to the field list.
